name: resvg
baseline: librsvg 2.50 (Cairo-based SVG renderer) and Inkscape 1.0 (also Batik 1.13/1.14 in the same table)
workload: Wikimedia SVG renderer evaluation: CPU time to render the W3C SVG test suite at 512 px (part of 337+1338+141 test files) with each renderer's command line tool, run in 2021 with resvg 0.14.0.
claimed_speedup: resvg 0.14.0: 1m 04.490s CPU time; librsvg 2.50: 1m 46.776s; Inkscape 1.0: 7m 57.465s; Batik: 6m 51.560s. Ratios (derived from snippet data): about 1.66x faster than librsvg, about 7.4x faster than Inkscape. Same table also gives correctness ratios: resvg 0.831, Inkscape 0.745, librsvg 0.662.
stars_or_usage: 4.1k stars; the CLI and C API are used by other projects (resvg-js, Wikimedia evaluation)
tradeoffs: Static SVG only (no scripting or animation). Rust crate with a C API (crates/c-api) so it is callable from C++. Renders on the CPU through tiny-skia; no GPU path. Built with a production profile (opt-level 3, LTO, one codegen unit).
caveats: Snippet only: the numbers come from the MediaWiki 'SVG benchmarks' page (https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/SVG_benchmarks, benchmark by a Wikimedia contributor, 2021) as quoted in a WebSearch result; the page itself is blocked here (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so benchmark_url is null and hardware, flags and exact command lines are unknown. The times are whole-test-suite CPU time of separate CLI processes, so process start-up is included. resvg 0.14.0 is far older than the current release. The resvg README itself carries no numbers and says that comparing performance between SVG renderers is like comparing apples and oranges; it only claims it is 'pretty fast' because it uses tiny-skia. Baselines are SVG renderers (librsvg is built on Cairo), not Skia, Cairo or Blend2D directly. Other resvg-based entries (resvg-js) are already recorded.
found_via: Blogs / talks: WebSearch 'SVG renderer benchmark resvg librsvg Inkscape rendering time faster blog' and follow-up 'mediawiki SVG benchmarks resvg librsvg Inkscape CPU time 337 files W3C test suite'; repo opened at github.com/linebender/resvg (README, Cargo.toml, commits).

name: Fast UI Draw (FastUIDraw)
baseline: Skia (OpenGL backend), Cairo (CPU renderer and OpenGL backend), Qt
workload: painter-cells demo: a table of 25x12 (600) cells, each cell clips a moving and rotating rectangle plus text to the cell; the demo was ported to Qt, Cairo and Skia for comparison (frame rate).
claimed_speedup: About 9x faster than Cairo's CPU renderer and several times faster than Qt, Cairo with OpenGL and Skia with OpenGL; 5x faster than Skia's GL backend in the rotation and clipping benchmark (as summarised in search results of the XDC 2016 talk and the Phoronix article).
tradeoffs: GPU-only canvas renderer: requires OpenGL 3.3 (optional OpenGL 4 extensions give better performance). Clipping and most state handling are left to the GPU, which is the source of the win on clip-heavy scenes. Repository is archived and Intel states it has ceased development.
caveats: Snippet only: the numbers are from Kevin Rogovin's XDC 2016 talk (x.org fast_ui_draw.pdf), a Phoronix article and a Chromium graphics-dev post, all blocked here (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so benchmark_url is null and hardware, compiler and flags are unknown. First-party numbers on one clipping-heavy demo; the repo has demos/painter_cells but the Qt, Cairo and Skia ports used for comparison were not found in it. A search summary of a Hacker News thread says it is the only renderer shown outperforming Skia but that the benchmarks were not representative. Compares GPU rendering against Cairo's CPU renderer for the 9x figure.
found_via: Blogs / talks: WebSearch 'FastUIDraw Intel benchmark Skia comparison canvas GPU performance' and '"Fast UI Draw" Intel Rogovin "times faster" Skia Cairo Qt benchmark rotation clipping'; repo opened at github.com/intel/fastuidraw (README, commits, demos folder).

name: muSkia Skia optimizer (Semantics for 2D Rasterization)
workload: Rasterization time of 99 Skia programs gathered from the top 100 websites, after an optimizer driven by a mechanized formal semantics of Skia (canvas state, layer stack, blending, color filters) rewrites them.
claimed_speedup: 18.7% speedup over Skia's most modern GPU backend on 99 Skia programs gathered from the top 100 websites (arXiv 2603.23696, Kulkarni, Whiting, Panchekha, March 2026, as quoted in a search result).
tradeoffs: It is an optimizer over Skia programs plus a formal semantics, not a replacement rasterizer; the gain depends on Skia command streams containing rewritable layer and blend patterns.
caveats: Snippet only: arXiv is blocked here, so the abstract was read from a WebSearch result and nothing else was opened; peer-review status, hardware, GPU model and Skia version are unknown. No code repository was found (guessed github.com/uwplse paths returned 404), so has_code is false until a verifier locates an artifact. The 18.7% figure is an aggregate over 99 programs, not a per-scene range.
found_via: Blogs / talks: WebSearch 'Show HN 2D vector graphics library faster than cairo OR faster than Skia single header software rasterizer benchmark' returned arxiv.org/pdf/2603.23696; WebSearch 'arxiv 2603.23696' gave the title and abstract snippet.
